message:
test(update): run both hops as real processes, and find the hang that only shows there

The primitive's own test drives every check inside one process. That
establishes the links. It does not establish that the chain runs, and it
cannot see the failures that exist only between processes.

Run across three processes and two pipes, one of those failures turned up
immediately: receive_credential had a deadline on connecting and none on
reading. A server that creates the pipe and then says nothing left the
receiver blocked for ever. In-process that never happens, because the other
side is always doing something. In the product it is an updater that hangs.
Both sides are overlapped with the same deadline now. The rule that a wait
needs a deadline had been applied to the sender and not to the receiver.

What is driven here: the chain delivering end to end; a bootstrap that dies
holding the credential, where hop 1 reports success and only the bootstrap's
own exit code says hop 2 never happened; a receiver that never acknowledges,
failing inside its deadline rather than hanging; and a parent that never
serves, where the bootstrap gives up and never starts a worker at all.

Each process writes its own command line and environment block, and the test
asserts the token appears nowhere except the line where the worker reports
what it received.

The helper is not updater_main. Running the real updater in a test would
have it copy itself into an administrators-only directory and stop product
processes. So the channel is verified between processes and the updater's
sequencing around it is not -- said in the helper's header as well as here,
because that distinction is the whole reason this file is worth reading.

It also passed alone and failed once in the full 62-suite run. Three
processes were appending to one file; the loser writes half a line, and half
a line reads as a missing one. A test that fails only under load gets called
flaky instead of read. One file per process now, and three consecutive clean
runs.
